title: His Right Hand Buttoned His Shirt, While His Own Left Hand Unbuttoned It
description:
What happens when your own hand executes smooth, purposeful actions you never consciously chose? In 1981, Gary Goldberg, Nathaniel Mayer, and Joseph Toglia coined the Alien Hand Sign after medial-frontal stroke patients lost the internal veto brake on automatic object grasping (Archives of Neurology, DOI: 10.1001/archneur.1981.00510110043004), and Todd Feinberg's 1992 classification separated frontal grasp release from callosal intermanual conflict—where one hand calmly unbuttons the shirt the other hand just buttoned.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Goldberg G, Mayer NH, Toglia JU (1981) Medial frontal cortex infarction and the alien hand sign. Archives of Neurology 38(11): 683-686. https://doi.org/10.1001/archneur.1981.00510110043004
- Biran I, Giovannetti T, Buxbaum L, Chatterjee A (2006) The alien hand syndrome: What makes the alien hand alien? Cognitive Neuropsychology 23(4): 563-582. https://doi.org/10.1080/02643290500180282
